If the generator is meant to be external, declare it in the project's external generator configuration so it is registered in context->extGen.

message: a single context must be specified
title: csolution: a single context must be specified
cause: The csolution generator command ran with zero or more than one selected build context, while ExecuteGenerator needs exactly one. The check at ProjMgrWorker.cpp:5102 counts m_selectedContexts, which is filled from the context names given on the command line, so the user either passed no context or passed several.
fix: Run the generator command for exactly one context, naming it as a project.context pair (for example <project>+<target>), so that m_selectedContexts holds a single entry. Run it once per context if several need generating.

message: access sequence pack was not loaded: '$Pack(<…>)$'
title: csolution: access sequence pack was not loaded: '$Pack(…)$'
cause: A `$Pack(vendor::name)$` access sequence in a csolution input (for example a path in a component or build setting) names a pack that no loaded pack matches. ExpandPackDir walks the loaded packs and compares each pack ID with the requested vendor and name; if none matches, the replacement stays empty. The `<…>` in the message is the pack reference as written, and the message repeats it wrapped in `$Pack(...)$`. The pack is probably not installed in the pack root, not listed in the required packs, or spelled differently from the installed pack.
fix: Check the `$Pack(...)$` argument against the pack that is actually installed, using the vendor::name form. Make sure the pack is declared under the project's packs or the solution's required packs, and install it with cpackget or the pack manager if it is missing. Then rerun the build. The source gives no other way to resolve it.
note: The warning is emitted through ProjMgrLogger::Warn and processing continues without replacing the sequence, so the item keeps its unexpanded $Pack(...)$ text. The cause is inferred from the matching loop; the source does not say which pack set is searched for the missing pack. The README does not document this message.

title: csolution: board mounted device … not found
cause: The board selected for the project lists a mounted device (name and vendor taken from the board's pack). When csolution looks that device up in the filtered device model built for the project, the lookup returns nothing, so the device the board mounts is not among the devices csolution has loaded. The placeholder is the full device name of that mounted device. The source does not show how the filtered model is populated, so the likely reason, that the pack providing that device is not installed or not part of the project's packs, is an inference.
fix: Check that the pack that defines the board's mounted device is installed. If it is missing, install it with cpackget add Vendor::PackName, using the vendor and pack that define the device. Then make sure the project's pack selection includes it. If the board is meant to use a different device, select it explicitly in the csolution YAML instead of relying on the board's mounted device.
note: The message is printed only when exactly one mounted device exists and it is missing from context.rteFilteredModel. The cause of the missing entry (missing pack versus filtering) is not shown in these lines. The README does not document this message.

message: cgen file was not found, run generator '<…>' for context '<…>'
title: csolution: cgen file was not found, run generator '…' for context '…'
cause: During csolution's generator import, the tool looks for the .cgen file named in the generator's options for a context. If that file does not exist on disk, it prints this error, with '<…>' filled by the generator id (options.id) and the context id. The cgen file is produced by running the generator, so it has not been generated yet for that context.
fix: Run the generator for the named context so the .cgen file is created, then run the csolution command again. Check that the generator id and context shown in the message match a generator in your project's configuration.
note: The message names the generator and context, but the source does not show which command runs the generator; the fix relies on the message wording. The code also stores the missing cgen path and returns a non-null clayer with success=false, so the failure is reported to the caller through the success flag.

message: component '<…>' does not accept more than <…> instance(s)
title: csolution: component '…' does not accept more than … instance(s)
cause: The csolution project requests more instances of a component than the component's definition allows. The requested count comes from the component's instances value in the csolution input (item.instances), and the limit is the maximum instance count the matched component declares in the pack description (GetMaxInstances()). The first placeholder is the component name from the request, and the number is the maximum the component accepts.
fix: Lower the instances value for this component in the csolution project (or in the layer or component entry that sets it) to at most the maximum printed in the message. If more instances are really needed, check whether a different component variant or a pack version declares a higher maximum; the limit itself is defined by the pack, not by csolution.
note: Not documented in the README. The message is printed only when item.instances exceeds GetMaxInstances(); the lines given do not show where item.instances is read from the YAML, so the exact input key is inferred rather than confirmed. Otherwise the handling is plain: an error is logged and the error flag is set, and no instances attribute is added.

The '<…>' in the message is the component name from the YAML, and the optional 'did you mean' text is that hint.

If the component comes from a pack that is not yet included, add that pack under packs in the project or the solution, then rebuild. Check that the pack is installed in the CMSIS pack root.

message: conflict: component '<…>' is listed multiple times
title: csolution: conflict: component '…' is listed multiple times
cause: AddComponent appends each component to the destination list only if no entry with the same component name is already there. When it finds a match and the caller did not set ignoreDuplicates, it logs this error and returns false. So the same component name (the '<…>' in the message) was collected twice for one context, for example through two component entries in the csolution project or through a layer that repeats a component already listed in the project. The lines given do not show the callers, so which input path produced the second entry is not confirmed.
fix: Find every place the named component is added for this context (the components list in the .csolution.yml or the .cproject.yml, and any clayer that declares it) and keep only one entry. If the same component has to come from several sources, give each entry a distinct filter so only one applies to a given context. Then rerun the csolution command.
note: The message is not documented in the README. The code is empty in the message. The ignoreDuplicates path prints a warning ('ignoring conflict') instead of this error, so the callers that pass true decide whether users see the error at all; those callers are outside the lines given. The fix above is a reading of the trigger and is not confirmed by a README entry.

message: conflict: file '<…>' is declared multiple times
title: csolution: conflict: file '…' is declared multiple times
cause: During group processing, AddFile compares each file already collected into the destination list against the file of the new source node, and fails when the same path string is found. This happens when the same file entry (after the file's path is stored as written in the csolution or cproject input) appears more than once within one group or across the files of the same group scope, for example the same source listed twice in a group's files or in both a group and a layer that contribute to the same group. The file name printed is the one already present in the list.
fix: Open the csolution or project file that lists the file and remove the duplicate entry, keeping it in only one group, or put it under a single group with a for-compiler or context filter so only one copy applies. Then run the build again.
note: The comparison is on the raw file string, so the same file written with different relative paths would not be flagged; the message is raised only for identical strings. The README does not document this message. The message reads 'file' but the check is in AddFile, which also handles file lists for groups.

message: conflict: group '<…>' is declared multiple times
title: csolution: conflict: group '…' is declared multiple times
cause: AddGroup compares each group in the destination list with the incoming group by its name (dstNode.group == src.group) among the groups already added at the same level. Two groups with the same name appear at the same nesting level of the project: the cproject groups, the clayer groups, or the groups nested inside one group, since each level is checked against its own list. The name in the message is the duplicated group name.
fix: Find every group with that name in the csolution project and its clayers and nested groups, then rename one of them or merge their files into a single group entry so each group name is unique at its level.
note: The message is printed with the group name, not the file path. The check runs only for groups whose filters and compiler match the context, so a duplicate under a non-matching condition is not reported. The README has no entry for this message, so the cause above is read from the source only.

message: context '<…>' generator '<…>' from component '<…>': gpdsc validation failed
title: csolution: context '…' generator '…' from component '…': gpdsc validation failed

The message names the context, the generator and the component that declared the gpdsc. The source lines shown do not include ReadGpdscFile, so the kind of validation failure is not visible here. Processing continues after this warning, unlike the 'reading gpdsc failed' error, which returns false.

Correct the reported problems in the gpdsc file, for example by regenerating it with the generator named in the message, then rebuild. If the gpdsc is not fixed, the components it provides are still added to the context, so check that the generated output is what you expect.
note: The README does not document this message. The validation error details are produced inside ProjMgrUtils::ReadGpdscFile, which is outside the lines given, so the specific failure is unknown. The warning does not stop processing, and the gpdsc pack is still attached at line 2904.

message: context '<…>' generator '<…>' from component '<…>': reading gpdsc failed
title: csolution: context '…' generator '…' from component '…': reading gpdsc failed
cause: ProcessGpdsc calls ProjMgrUtils::ReadGpdscFile for each generator gpdsc file that a context uses. When that call returns no package, the tool cannot load the gpdsc file named in the message, so it logs this error and stops processing the context. The quoted context name, generator and component come from the context's gpdsc entry, and the gpdsc file path is passed as the logger's file argument. The source lines shown do not reveal which read step fails, so the exact reason (missing file, unreadable file or malformed content) is not confirmed here. A file that is readable but fails validation only produces the separate 'gpdsc validation failed' warning, not this error.

If the file is missing, correct the component or pack setup that refers to the generator so that the pack containing the gpdsc is installed. Then rerun the csolution command. The source lines do not show a further workaround.
note: The message is not documented in the README. The trigger is a null return from ProjMgrUtils::ReadGpdscFile, and its implementation is not in the lines given, so the file-level causes listed are a reading, not confirmed behaviour.

message: context '<…>' referenced by access sequence '<…>' does not exist or is not selected
title: csolution: context '…' referenced by access sequence '…' does not exist or is not selected
cause: An access sequence such as $Dname(contextName)$ in a csolution file names a context (project or build context) that FindReferencedContext cannot resolve among the selected contexts. The context name in the message is the referenced name as written in the sequence, and the sequence name is the access sequence that refers to it. Either the name is misspelled or partial, or the referenced context is not part of the solution's selected contexts (for example, it is not listed in the solution or is filtered out by the selected build types or target types).
fix: Check the context name inside the access sequence against the project and build type names in the csolution file, and correct any typo or partial name. Make sure the referenced context is listed in the solution and is selected by the build type, target type or other selection in use, so that it is part of the selected contexts. Then run the csolution command again.

The exact matching rules of FindReferencedContext are not in the lines given, so the cause of 'not selected' is inferred from the name lookup against m_selectedContexts. At solution level a separate message ('is not compatible') is printed earlier when no context name contains the referenced name at all, at line 3746.

message: context '<…>' referenced by access sequence '<…>' is not compatible
title: csolution: context '…' referenced by access sequence '…' is not compatible
cause: The access sequence in a solution-level csolution file references a context (for example '$Source(<name>)$' style sequence with a context argument) by a name fragment, and no context in the loaded set contains that fragment as a substring. Solution-level processing requires the referenced context name to match a known compatible context, so the lookup finds nothing and the tool stops. The '<…>' context value is the referenced name from the access sequence, and the sequence name is the access sequence being expanded.
fix: Check the access sequence in the solution's csolution.yml or the project file that names the context, and correct the context name so it matches a context that the solution actually defines (for example a project and build-type/target combination such as project+target). Make sure that context is part of the solution and compatible with its target and type settings, then run the build again.
note: The README does not document this message. The cause is inferred from the substring match over m_contexts at solution level; the exact syntax of the access sequence with a context argument is not shown in the lines given, so the fix describes checking the name rather than a specific option.

message: cproject not parsed, adding context failed
title: csolution: cproject not parsed, adding context failed

The cproject file named in the message (the cprojectFile argument) was therefore never read or parsed, most likely because it is missing from the csolution, misspelled, or was not loaded before the context was requested.

The source does not show a further workaround beyond making the cproject parse successfully.

The exact reason the file was not parsed is not visible in these lines; the cause above is an inference from the lookup and the branch. The README does not document this message.

title: csolution: debug-adapters.yml file not found
cause: RunListDebuggers gets the debug-adapters file path from GetDebugAdaptersFile() and stops with this error when that path is empty. The lines given do not show how GetDebugAdaptersFile() searches for the file, so the reason it comes back empty (no file in the expected location, or a missing installation component) is not visible here.

title: csolution: destination directory cannot be created
cause: csolution is about to write a generated YAML file (for example a generated .cbuild or .cprj style output) to the given path and the file content differs from what is on disk, so updating is allowed. Before writing, it calls RteFsUtils::MakeSureFilePath on the target path to create its parent directories, and that call failed. The path in the message is the generated file whose parent directory could not be created, typically because a path component exists as a regular file, or the location is not writable.
fix: Check the output location shown in the message: make sure no file exists where one of its parent directories should be, and that the parent directory is writable by the user running csolution. Remove or rename the conflicting file or fix the permissions, then rerun the build. The source gives no further workaround.

title: csolution: export file cannot be written
cause: During convert, after the regular cprj for a context has been written, the tool also writes a non-locked export copy named <context name><export suffix>.cprj into that context's cprj directory. This message is printed when GenerateCprj fails for that export path, so the file or its directory could not be written. The source does not show the underlying I/O error, so the exact reason (permissions, invalid path, full disk) is not visible from these lines.
fix: Check that the cprj output directory of the context is writable and that the export suffix yields a valid file name, then re-run the convert command. The source gives no other workaround; if the error persists, check the directory permissions and the path for the export file directly.
note: The regular cprj write failure at ProjMgr.cpp:802 prints a different message ("file cannot be written"). This export path is only reached when m_export is non-empty and m_cbuildgen is set. The README does not document this message.

message: failed to load and insert packs
title: csolution: failed to load and insert packs
cause: This message is a wrapper printed when the pack kernel fails to load the collected PDSC files. LoadAllRelevantPacks gathers the PDSC files from the selected contexts and from installed packs (via GetEffectivePdscFiles), then calls LoadAndInsertPacks. The kernel's own error for the specific pack or PDSC that failed, such as a malformed or unreadable PDSC or a pack that cannot be parsed, is logged before this line and is not repeated here. Because LoadPacks defers the return on this failure, the build still continues to the context checks before exiting.
fix: Read the error lines printed just before this one, which name the PDSC file or pack that failed to load, and fix that pack. Typically this means repairing or reinstalling the named pack so its .pdsc file is well-formed, and checking that the pack is installed in the pack root the build uses. Then rerun the csolution command.
note: The message carries no variable part, so it cannot identify the failing pack by itself; the specific cause is only in the kernel's earlier output. CheckRteErrors() decides the return value, so the build may not stop at this line. The README does not document this message.

message: failed to read latest pack information from pack index
title: csolution: failed to read latest pack information from pack index
cause: The pack version check (CheckPackVerAndCollectRelNotes) asks the kernel to build a map of the latest available version and PDSC path for each pack from the pack index. ReadPackLatestVerAndPath returned false, so the check stops before it reads any project packs. The lines shown do not include ReadPackLatestVerAndPath, so the specific reason it failed (missing or unreadable pack index, pack root not set up) is not visible here.
fix: Check that the CMSIS pack root has a readable pack index, meaning the .Index files and the .pdsc files they reference are present and not corrupted. If the index is missing or stale, refresh the installed packs with the CMSIS pack tooling (for example cpackget update-index or cpackget add for the needed packs) and run the check again. The source lines given do not show which index file or path the kernel reads, so confirm that location in ReadPackLatestVerAndPath before going further.
note: The message is printed only when ReadPackLatestVerAndPath returns false; the reason it fails is in code not shown. The README does not document this message. The fix about cpackget commands is a general suggestion and is not confirmed by the lines given.

message: file '<…>.base' not found; base version unknown
title: csolution: file '….base' not found; base version unknown
cause: During the PLM (Pack Lifecycle Management) check, csolution has found the component file instance in the project directory, but the copy of that file's base version, named with the suffix .base@<version> where <version> is the file's semantic version from the RTE, is not there. The message prints the instance path followed by '.base' without the version suffix that the existence check actually tests. The check sets the file's PLM status to missing base and continues, so the build is not stopped.
fix: Restore the missing base copy next to the file instance, or let csolution recreate the RTE-managed files by running the command with --update-rte, then rebuild. The source does not show a separate option for the base copy, so if the message persists after --update-rte, check that the file instance and its version in the pack are consistent.
note: The message text omits the @<version> part that the existence check at line 2407 tests, so the file named in the log is not the exact path checked. The --update-rte hint comes from the missing-instance message at line 2394, not from this warning; that the same fix applies here is my reading. This is a warning, not an error.

title: csolution: file cannot be written
cause: During RunConvert, csolution builds the output path <cprj directory>/<context name>.cprj and calls m_generator.GenerateCprj for it. When that call returns false, the tool prints this error with the context name and file path and stops. The source does not show the underlying write error, and the result of RteFsUtils::CreateDirectories on the cprj directory is ignored, so a missing or unwritable output directory, or a path that cannot be created, is a likely reason.
fix: Check that the cprj output directory exists or can be created, is not blocked by a file of the same name, and is writable by the current user. Confirm the path printed in the message is valid, then rerun csolution. If the directory is fine, the source gives no further step; check the permissions and disk space of the printed path.
note: The message is printed only when GenerateCprj returns false, and the generator's reason is not logged in these lines. The cause given is an inference from the directory creation and path setup around the trigger, not a confirmed failure mode. The README does not document this message.

message: file not allowed to be updated
title: csolution: file not allowed to be updated
cause: WriteFile generated the YAML content for a file that already exists and differs from it, so CompareFile returned false. The caller passed allowUpdate as false, which forbids overwriting an existing file, so the write is refused. The message names the file (%NAME% is the filename argument) and the context of the operation.
fix: Check whether the listed file is a generated file that csolution should be allowed to rewrite. If it is a generated file you no longer need, remove it and run the command again so it is created fresh. If you edited it by hand, move your changes into the source input or revert the file, then run the command again. The lines shown do not identify which caller passes allowUpdate as false, so the exact option that enables the update is not established here.
note: The README does not document this message. The lines given do not show the callers that pass allowUpdate, so the option that sets it and the exact reason a caller forbids the update remain unverified. The cause is a reading of the trigger condition.

title: csolution: found multiple device variants
cause: The message is printed when the device the project resolved to is a parent device that has device variants under it (RteDeviceItem::VARIANT items), so the selection is not a single concrete device. The device comes either from the device name given in the csolution file (matched against full device names in the installed packs, lines 1455-1478) or, when none is given, from the device mounted on the selected board (lines 1495-1500). Because the matched device still has variant items, the tool stops. The wording says 'multiple' but the code does not count matches. It reports that a variant must be chosen.
fix: Set the device in the csolution project to one of the variant full names that the tool lists right after this message (the lines starting with 'one of the following device variants must be specified:'). Use the exact full device name, for example Vendor::Device:Variant, rather than the base device name. If the device came from a board, set the device explicitly to the variant that matches your hardware, because the board's mounted device has no variant chosen.
note: The message text ('found multiple device variants') does not match the check, which only tests whether the device has variant items. The list of variants is printed by a second error on line 1509. If neither deviceItem.name nor a board mounted device is set, matchedDevice stays null and line 1503 dereferences it without a check, which may crash; this path is not confirmed from the lines given.

title: csolution: found no mounted device
cause: The csolution matched a board, but the board's pack entry lists no mounted devices, so GetMountedDevices returns an empty list. The code at line 1439 treats an empty list as an error no matter whether the user also named a device, so the message appears whenever the selected board declares no mounted device.
fix: Check the board entry in the installed board pack for a mounted device declaration. If it has none, select a board that declares mounted devices, or correct the board pack. Then rerun the csolution command. Do not rely on adding a device name alone to clear this error, because the zero-device check does not depend on the device setting.
note: The enclosing block condition is not in the lines given, so the exact entry path is inferred. The trigger is the zero-size branch, and it is reached regardless of deviceItem.name, which the other branch at line 1432 checks. The README does not document this message.

title: csolution: generator '…' is not dry-run capable
cause: The csolution command was run with the dry-run option, and the selected generator's IsDryRunCapable check returned false for its executable. The generator is identified by the <…> id in the message, and the check only passes when the generator declares dry-run support, so a generator without that support cannot be run in dry-run mode.
fix: Run the generator without the dry-run option so it executes normally, or use a generator that declares dry-run capability. The source does not show how a generator declares that capability, so check the generator's own documentation or its package definition for dry-run support.
note: The message is printed only when m_dryRun is set and the generator reports it is not dry-run capable. The README does not document this message. The cause is inferred from the trigger; how IsDryRunCapable decides is not in the lines given.

message: generator '<…>' required by component '<…>' was not found in global register
title: csolution: generator '…' required by component '…' was not found in global register
cause: A component in the csolution project or its packs names a code generator by id, and the csolution tool cannot find a generator with that id in its global generator register. The lookup goes through ProjMgrKernel's external generator table, which is populated from installed packs and the CMSIS environment; a generator id that is not registered there fails the check. The first quoted value is the generator id from the component, the second is the component id that requires it.
fix: Check the generator id spelled in the component's generator reference against the generator ids the installed packs declare, and correct the spelling if it differs. If the generator comes from a pack, make sure that pack is installed and selected in the project so that its generator is registered before the build runs, for example by running cpackget to install the pack and then rebuilding.
note: The source confirms the trigger, which is a failed lookup in the kernel's external generator table. The user-facing cause (misspelled id or missing pack) is my reading of how that table is filled; the lines given do not show where the table is populated. The message is printed with severity error and no README entry exists for it.

title: csolution: generator '…' was not found
cause: ExecuteGenerator processes the selected context and then looks up the requested generator id in context.generators. The message is printed when that id is not among the generators the context resolved, so the id given to the run does not match any generator declared for the project's components, gpdsc files, or selected context.
fix: Use a generator id exactly as the pack declares it, and make sure the pack providing that generator is part of the project and the selected context. Check the spelling and case of the id against the generator entries in the pack's PDSC and in the project's gpdsc or component files. Then run again with the corrected id.
note: The lines do not show how generatorId is supplied to ExecuteGenerator, so the exact command-line option is not named here. The lookup relies on context.generators being filled by ProcessContext, which is not in the lines given. Other messages in this function, such as 'generator executable ... was not found', use the same wording but are triggered by a different check.

title: csolution: generator executable '…' was not found
cause: The generator with id generatorId was found in the context's generators, but GetExecutable(context.rteActiveTarget) returned an empty path for the active target. This means the generator's package definition (PDSC) does not give an executable for the selected target, so there is nothing to check for existence or permissions. The '<…>' in the message is the generator id the user asked to run.
fix: Check that the generator entry in the PDSC of the pack that provides it declares an executable for the target in use, and that the pack providing the generator is installed and selected for the context. Then rerun the generator command. The source lines give no further fix beyond this.
note: The message text is the same as the one in the code path only when the executable is empty; the message does not name the executable or the target. The condition is read from the lines given; the README entry does not document this message.

message: generator executable file '<…>' does not exist
title: csolution: generator executable file '…' does not exist
cause: The csolution run selected a generator whose executable path, resolved for the active target, is not present on disk. The generator comes from a pack's generator definition, and the path printed is the value of generator->GetExecutable(context.rteActiveTarget); the check runs after the cbuild generation step and before the executable permission check.
fix: Check that the generator's executable is installed in the pack cache: confirm the pack providing the generator is installed (for example with cpackget or by re-running the csolution command so the required packs are fetched), and that the path printed in the message exists. If the path points into a pack, make sure the pack version in the csolution project matches an installed pack version.

message: generator file '<…>' cannot be executed, check permissions

The path is the generator's executable as resolved in ExecuteGenerator via generator->GetExecutable(context.rteActiveTarget); the check runs after the existence check, so the file is present but lacks execute permission.
fix: Check the file's permissions on the reported path (for example with ls -l) and make it executable for the current user, e.g. chmod +x on that file, then rerun the generator command. If the file came from a pack, reinstall or re-extract the pack so the executable bit is restored.

The cause is inferred from the existence check preceding this one; the source does not show how IsExecutableFile determines executability, so a filesystem or platform-specific reason (such as a non-executable file type) is not excluded by the lines given.

title: csolution: generator identifier was not specified
cause: The csolution run reached the code generator path (RunCodeGenerator) without a generator identifier, so m_codeGenerator is empty. The tool checks this before it parses any input, so the csolution.yml content is not the cause; the command line that selected the generator mode did not supply an identifier for the generator to run.
fix: Re-run the command and pass the generator identifier that the code generator mode expects, for example the identifier of a generator defined in your project's generator configuration. Check the csolution command help for the exact option that sets the generator identifier, since the source lines shown do not name it.

message: generator output directory was not set
title: csolution: generator output directory was not set
cause: The csolution tool resolves the output directory of an external generator in GetExtGeneratorOptions. It takes the path from the 'generators' node of the layer, project or solution (a path set for that generator id, or a baseDir), and if that is empty it falls back to the global generator register by generator id. If the result is still empty, the tool logs this error and stops. This means the generator used by the project has no output directory: neither the generators node in the csolution or cproject YAML sets one, nor the generator's global registration provides one.
fix: Give the generator an output directory in the csolution YAML, for example under a 'generators' node of the project or solution: set a path for the generator id, or set a baseDir so the tool builds the path from the generator id. Then run the build again. If the generator is supposed to be registered globally, check that its global registration (done by the generator's own installation) provides a path.

The global register lookup is in m_extGenerator->GetGlobalGenDir, which is outside the lines given.

message: ignoring conflict: component '<…>' is listed multiple times
title: csolution: ignoring conflict: component '…' is listed multiple times
cause: AddComponent found a component already in the destination list for the same context, with the same component identifier as the new entry. The caller passed ignoreDuplicates as true, so the tool keeps the earlier entry, skips the new one and prints the warning. The '<…>' is the component identifier string (the component's Cclass::Cgroup form) that is listed more than once. The source does not show which caller sets ignoreDuplicates or which input file produced the second listing.

Then rerun the csolution command and check that the warning is gone. If the same component is required through several layers or dependencies, check that only one of them adds it explicitly.

The warning is therefore the lenient variant, and the build continues with the first entry. The message has no code. The README does not document this message. title: csolution: initializing RTE Model failed
cause: ProjMgrWorker::InitializeModel obtained the kernel from ProjMgrKernel::Get() successfully, but the kernel's GetGlobalModel() returned a null pointer. The csolution tool therefore cannot create the RTE model that holds the packs and project data it needs to continue. The source lines do not show what makes the global model creation fail, so the trigger is internal to the tool rather than a particular user input.

Check that the csolution tool installation is complete and not corrupted, and that the CMSIS pack root (CMSIS_PACK_ROOT or the default location) is accessible, then rerun the command. If the message persists, report it to the CMSIS devtools project with the csolution version and the command line.

The trigger is a null-pointer check on m_model right after the kernel is created, so the failure is internal and the README-style advice on the pack root is my guess at likely causes, not something the source shows. Kernel creation failure is reported separately with 'initializing RTE Kernel failed' at line 506.

title: csolution: invalid pattern '…': …
cause: The csolution parser handles a type filter string (a for-context or not-for-context entry, from a YAML value such as a build or target type list) as a regex when it starts with '^' or '\' (the first '^' or '\' is at position 0). It compiles the whole string with std::regex, and the C++ regex engine rejected it. The '<…>' in the message is the offending filter string as written in the YAML, and the appended text is the regex engine's error description (e.g. an unbalanced parenthesis or invalid escape).
fix: Correct the regular expression in the reported filter so that it compiles as an ECMAScript regex. Check for unbalanced parentheses or brackets, and for backslash escapes that are not valid regex syntax; a literal backslash must be written as '\\' in the YAML. If a plain name was intended rather than a pattern, remove the leading '^' or '\' and use the '.' (build) or '+' (target) prefix form instead.
note: The message text is 'invalid pattern' followed by the regex_error what() string, so the exact regex problem is only known from that suffix. The README does not document this message. The cause is inferred from the trigger; the lines given do not show which regex dialect the std::regex default uses.

message: linker script template for compiler '<…>' was not found
title: csolution: linker script template for compiler '…' was not found
cause: csolution looks for a default linker script template when the context has no linker script set and it is not a dry run. It walks the compiler root directory recursively and matches a file whose double-stem equals '<toolchain name>_linker_script' (case-insensitive). The message is printed when no such file exists under the compiler root, so the toolchain named in the context (the '<...>' part of the message) has no bundled linker script template. In that case csolution does not set a linker script and returns without copying anything.
fix: Set the linker script explicitly in the csolution project (linker script entry of the build-type or project YAML) so csolution does not need a default template. Alternatively, check that the selected toolchain is installed in the expected compiler root, since a missing template in that root is what triggers the warning.
note: The message is a warning and processing continues without a linker script; the user-facing cause is my reading of the directory scan. The README does not document this message.

message: loaded pack '<…>' does not match specified metadata '<…>'
title: csolution: loaded pack '…' does not match specified metadata '…'
cause: During LoadAllRelevantPacks, csolution compares each loaded pack's version suffix (the part after '+' in its version string) with the metadata value recorded for that pack ID in m_packMetadata. When the two differ, it prints this warning, with the first placeholder being the pack ID plus its version and the second being the metadata value the user's input specified. The warning is only raised when the pack ID has a metadata entry, so the user's input must have supplied a metadata value for that pack, and the installed or loaded pack carries a different '+' suffix.
fix: Check the pack version and metadata specified for that pack in the csolution project against the pack actually installed. Either align the pack's version (the '+' suffix) with the specified metadata, for example by installing the matching pack version, or update the metadata in the project to the version suffix that is actually loaded. The source does not show a further automatic resolution, so this is a manual correction.
note: The message is a warning and the function still returns true, so processing continues. The first placeholder is built by concatenating GetPackageID(false) and GetVersionString() without a separator, so the printed pack name and version may run together. The README does not document this message.

title: csolution: malformed access sequence: '…
cause: The csolution tool scans the item string for access sequences delimited by '$' (for example $Pack(vendor::name)$ or $OutDir(context)$). When RteUtils::GetAccessSequence cannot find a complete sequence while it walks the string, it prints this error and aborts processing of that item. The text after the quote is the whole item as it was passed in (the variable-expanded value when the item is not solution-level), so the unpaired or unterminated '$' is somewhere in that value.
fix: Find the value shown after the quote in the csolution YAML or the PDSC/project setting that produced it. Check that every access sequence opens and closes with '$' and has balanced parentheses, for example $Pack(Vendor::Name)$, and remove or escape any stray '$' that is not meant as a sequence delimiter. Then rerun the csolution command.
note: The message has no closing quote, so the printed value is the full item and may be long. The exact delimiter rules live in RteUtils::GetAccessSequence, which is not among the lines given, so the cause is inferred from the call site. The message has no code and the README does not document it.

title: csolution: manifest file does not exist
cause: GetToolboxVersion searches the CMSIS-Toolbox directory (the toolboxDir argument, from GetCmsisToolboxDir) non-recursively for a file matching manifest_<major.minor.patch>*.yml. This is reached only when a csolution file has a created-for entry naming cmsis-toolbox at a version; ValidateCreatedFor calls GetToolboxVersion to compare that version with the installed toolbox. If no such manifest file is in the toolbox directory, the version cannot be determined and the check is skipped. The path shown in the message is the toolbox directory that was searched.
fix: Check that the toolbox directory shown in the message contains a manifest_<version>.yml file of the installed CMSIS-Toolbox. If the toolbox installation is incomplete or was not set up correctly, reinstall or repair it so that the manifest file is present. If the created-for entry in the csolution file is not needed, remove it so this check is not run.
note: The warning is not fatal: GetToolboxVersion returns an empty string and ValidateCreatedFor then returns true, so processing continues without the version comparison. The cause and fix are inferred from the code path; the README does not document this message. The reference to removing created-for is a workaround I derived from the code, not an officially documented remedy.

title: csolution: missing RTE target
cause: ProcessComponents() needs the RTE active target of the build context to resolve the components a project requires. When rteActiveTarget is null, it logs 'missing RTE target' and returns failure before any component is matched. The given lines do not show where rteActiveTarget is assigned, so the reason it stays unset is not established here. It most likely means the target for this context could not be set up, for example because the device, target type or required packs were not resolved.
fix: The source lines do not show a direct user-side fix. Check the log above this message for earlier errors about the device, board, target type or packs of this project, and resolve those first. Then confirm that the packs the project uses are installed and that the csolution project refers to a valid device or target, and run the build again.
note: The message has no code and the README does not document it. The assignment of rteActiveTarget lies outside the given lines, so the upstream cause is inferred and not confirmed. The message is logged without the context name, so it does not say which project or target failed.

title: csolution: missing device and/or board info
cause: ProcessDevice runs for a build context whose csolution input names neither a board nor a device. GetDeviceItem fills deviceItem from context.device, and the check fails when context.board is empty and deviceItem.name is empty. The project or target therefore has no device and no board to resolve against, so the tool stops with this error for that context. The context name is passed as the second argument, so the log line identifies which context is affected.
fix: Give the project or target a device or a board in its csolution YAML, for example a device: entry naming the part number, or a board: entry naming a board that the installed packs provide. Make sure the device or board name is spelled as the pack declares it, since an unresolved device name leaves deviceItem.name empty as well. Then rerun csolution.
note: The README does not document this message. The cause is inferred from the trigger condition only; the exact YAML key that feeds context.device and context.board is not shown in the lines given, so the fix names the keys by their usual meaning and should be checked against the schema.

message: mlops: <…>no default unnamed target set for '<…>'<…>target set '<…>' not found<…>
title: csolution: mlops: …no default unnamed target set for '…'…target set '…' not found…
cause: The mlops section of the csolution YAML names a target type (the mlops target string is 'type' or 'type@set') for which no target set can be picked. When the target set part is empty, the tool looks for a default unnamed target set: a target set whose debugger is Arm-FVP when the simulator default is used, or any non-Arm-FVP one for hardware. The message's '<target type>' is the type named in the mlops entry, and it appears because the type exists but none of its target sets matches that default rule.
fix: Check the target-type definition in the csolution YAML for the named target type and make sure it has a target set matching the default (an Arm-FVP debugger for simulation, a non-FVP debugger for hardware). Alternatively, name the target set explicitly in the mlops target as 'type@set' using a set name that exists in that target type.
note: The message text uses the target type for the '<…>' slot in the unnamed case, so the wording 'for <type>' refers to the target type, not a set name. The lookup that fails here is GetTargetSetItemRef called with no set name, and the rule it applies (Arm-FVP debugger versus other) is read from the source. The README does not document this message; the cause and fix are my reading of the source and the exact user-facing wording may need checking against a real build.

message: mlops: no image or project-context specified for target '<…>'
title: csolution: mlops: no image or project-context specified for target '…'
cause: The csolution's mlops section names a hardware or simulator target type, but no image entry or project-context matching that target produced a context. CollectSettings builds context names from each target set image's context (or the solution name) plus '+' and the target type, and looks them up among the loaded contexts. When the lookup finds none for a target that was explicitly given, the tool reports the error. The '<…>' in the message is the target type, with '@' and the target set appended when one is given.
fix: Check the mlops hardware/simulator target entries in the csolution YAML against the target-types and target-set definitions. Make sure the referenced target type has an image in the target set, or a project-context whose name matches the context the tool builds, and that the target type and target set spellings match. Then re-run csolution.
note: The README does not document this message. The cause is inferred from the context-name lookup in the source; the exact user-facing YAML layout that makes the match succeed is not shown in the lines given.

message: more than one valid <serialwire> element found
title: csolution: more than one valid <serialwire> element found
cause: The device's effective trace properties contain more than one <serialwire> sink element without a Pname attribute. The loop at lines 580-603 counts every such sink, and when the count is greater than one the tool warns, since only the first serial-wire sink is kept in the debug topology. The warning is about the device/pack description (PDSC device trace elements) rather than the csolution project file itself.
fix: Check the device or board PDSC trace definitions for the device, and keep a single <serialwire> element per processor (without a Pname attribute, since Pname-tagged traces are ignored). If several are declared for different processors, give them a Pname attribute so they are skipped here. If the pack is not yours, report the duplicate to the pack vendor.
note: The README does not document this message. The message is a warning, not an error, and the tool continues. The cause is inferred from the counting logic; which PDSC element produces the duplicate is not visible in the lines given.

title: csolution: multiple cdefault files were found
cause: GetCdefaultFile searches the project root directory and, if set, the compiler root for files matching cdefault.yml or cdefault.yaml. The message is printed when RteFsUtils::FindFileRegEx returns false but has already filled cdefaultFile with a path, which indicates that more than one matching cdefault file was found. The printed path is the value stored in cdefaultFile, so it names one of the matching files.
fix: Keep exactly one cdefault.yml (or cdefault.yaml) in the search locations. Check the project root directory and the compiler root (the toolchain directory reported by the tool) for extra copies, and remove or rename the duplicates. Then run the csolution command again.
note: The behaviour of FindFileRegEx when it returns false is not in the lines given, so the reading that a duplicate match is the cause is inferred from the message text and the call. The third argument is a file path, so the message reports a path, not the name of a directory. The search covers the compiler root as well as the project directory, so a stray cdefault file in the toolchain tree can also trigger it.

message: no board was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no board was found with filter '…'
cause: The user asked csolution to list boards with a filter (the list-boards command takes a filter argument) and none of the installed boards matched it. ListBoards collects every board from the selected contexts' filtered models, formats each as Vendor::Name[:Revision] (Pack), applies the filter terms to that list, and reports this error when nothing is left. The '<…>' in the message is the filter string the user passed.
fix: Run the list command without a filter to see the exact board names and vendor strings that are installed, then retry with a term that matches one of them. Install the pack that provides the board if it is missing, for example with cpackget. Check that the context or target selection is the one that holds the board, since only selected contexts are searched.
note: The README does not document this message. The cause and fix are read from ListBoards; the exact filter syntax is handled by RteUtils::ApplyFilter, which is not in the lines given. The sibling message for devices at line 4346 has the same structure.

message: no compatible software layer found. Review required connections of the project
title: csolution: no compatible software layer found. Review required connections of the project
cause: This message is printed by the list-layers command path (RunListLayers) when m_worker.ListLayers fails to detect a compatible software layer for at least one context. It is emitted once per failed context, so the context name is attached as the second argument. The text itself does not name the layer or the connection; it only says the project's required connections need review, which points at the project's component selections or layer requirements not matching any available layer.
fix: Run the layer listing again on the csolution.yml and check the connections of each failed context: confirm that the components and layers required by the project are provided by the packs that are installed and referenced, and that the selected target/context matches what the layers were built for. Then rerun the command. The source gives no further automatic remedy, so review of the project's connections is the step to take.
note: The README does not document this message. The source only shows the trigger and the per-context reporting; the specific reasons ListLayers fails are not in the given lines, so the cause is an interpretation of the message text.

message: no component was found for device '<…>'
title: csolution: no component was found for device '…'
cause: The csolution list components command loaded the packs for the selected context and resolved its target, but the active target reports no installed components after filtering. The device named in the message is the context's device value as resolved for that context, so the message names the device whose component set came back empty. The source only shows that the device had no components; it does not show the specific reason the filter removed them.
fix: Check that the device name in the csolution project (or the --context selection) matches a device that exists in the installed packs, and that the packs providing it are installed (for example with cpackget or csolution's pack update). Then rerun the list command.
note: The message is printed only when the context name is non-empty; an empty context gets the 'no installed component was found' message instead. README does not document this message.

message: no component was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no component was found with filter '…'
cause: The csolution `list components` operation was given a filter argument, and none of the component IDs of the installed components of the selected contexts match it. The component IDs are collected from the active target's filtered components after the packs are loaded and the target attributes are set, and the filter is applied to that list with the split filter terms; an empty result yields this error. The '<…>' in the message is the filter string the user passed.
fix: Check the filter spelling and the terms it uses against the component list the tool prints without a filter, then run the command again with the corrected filter. Also confirm that the required packs are installed and that the context (device/target) selected is the one that provides the components you expect.
note: The README does not document this message. The cause is inferred from the ListComponents code path: the message fires only when a filter is given and no component ID matches, so an empty component set without a filter gives a different message ('no component was found for device' or 'no installed component was found') instead.

message: no context was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no context was found with filter '…'
cause: ListContexts applies the user's filter string, split on commas into a set, to the project's ordered context names (m_ymlOrderedContexts) and finds none that match. The printed text is the filter as given. The filter is matched against context names, so a misspelled name, a wrong build-type or target part, or a context that is not defined in the project's csolution or cproject files will leave the result empty. The lines shown do not reveal which command option supplies the filter.
fix: Re-run the same command without the filter to see the context names the project actually defines, then pass one of those names exactly as printed. Check the spelling and the separators in the filter against that list.
note: The source lines show the filter application and the error, but not the calling command or the exact context name format. The sibling message 'no target-set was found with filter' at ProjMgrWorker.cpp:4869 follows the same pattern. Code field was empty in the input.

message: no default rwx memory nor algorithm with ramstart/size was found
title: csolution: no default rwx memory nor algorithm with ramstart/size was found
cause: CheckDefaultRam is called with a default RAM descriptor whose size is zero, meaning the tool found no RAM region for the debug target. The message names the two places it looks: a memory with rwx access in the device description, or a flash programming algorithm that defines ramstart and size. The source lines given do not show how defaultRam is filled, so the exact input that leaves it empty is inferred from the trigger, not confirmed.
fix: Check the device or board pack that the csolution project uses. Confirm that its PDSC describes a memory with rwx access, or a flash algorithm with ramstart and ramsize, that covers the RAM the debugger should use. If the pack has none, the device data is incomplete and needs a pack that defines it, or a corrected device selection in the csolution project. The source lines given do not show a further setting to change.
note: The README does not document this message. The trigger and the error text are clear in the source, but the path from PDSC or SVD input to the RamType size is outside the lines given, so the cause of the zero size is inferred.

title: csolution: no installed NPU was found
cause: The csolution `list npus` path (ListNpus) collects NPU information from the selected contexts after loading packs and applying the target attributes. If no context yields any NPU entry, the map of NPU info is empty and the tool reports that no installed NPU was found. The source lines show only the empty check and the collection loop; they do not show which packs or NPU entries the user lacks.
fix: Check that the packs providing NPU (Ethos-U) support are installed for the selected context, for example by running `cpackget list` or checking the CMSIS pack cache, and then run the list command again. The source gives no specific command, so treat this as a suggestion to verify the installation.
note: The message is not documented in the README. The message text says 'installed NPU', but the code only checks whether any NPU info was collected from the contexts, so the cause could also be a target or filter that matches no NPU. The filtered variant ('no NPU was found with filter') is a separate message printed at line 4436.

title: csolution: no installed board was found
cause: ListBoards loads the packs for each selected context, then collects every board in that context's filtered RTE model. The message is printed when that collection is empty across all selected contexts, so no board from the installed packs matched the selected contexts. The check runs after LoadPacks has succeeded, so the packs were read but none supplied a board.
fix: Install a pack that provides boards (for example a Device or BSP pack with board definitions) into the CMSIS pack root, then run the board listing again. Check that the contexts selected for the command are the ones whose packs supply boards. If a pack is already installed, confirm that its PDSC lists boards and that the project's pack selection does not exclude it.
note: The message says 'installed' but the check is on the filtered model of the selected contexts, not on the pack root, so a board can be missing because of context selection or filtering rather than a missing installation. The README does not document this message. The fix is my reading of the code path, not a documented procedure.

title: csolution: no installed component was found
cause: The csolution list components command (ListComponents) ran for a context with no device selected (empty selectedContext, i.e. no target-device context was named) and the active target's filtered component set came back empty. That means none of the installed packs provided components that match the project's filters for that unnamed context. The message is the no-device counterpart of 'no component was found for device', which is printed when a device context is named.
fix: Check that the packs providing the components are installed and visible to csolution (for example with cpackget list or by checking the pack root), and that the csolution project's packs and target settings select a device/board whose packs are present. If you want the list for a specific device, name that context on the command line so the device-specific message is shown and the device's packs can be inspected.
note: The message is printed only when selectedContext is empty; the trigger line 4466 is the else branch of that check. The README does not document this message. The exact reason the filtered set is empty is not visible in the lines given, so the cause above is an inference from the branch structure.

title: csolution: no installed device was found
cause: The csolution list devices command builds its list from the device items in the filtered RTE model of each selected context, after loading the packs for that context. When no installed pack provides a device leaf (a device entry with no sub-items), the set stays empty and the tool prints this message. The filter argument is applied only after this check, so a filter cannot cause this message.
fix: Install the device pack(s) that provide the devices you want to list, then run the list command again. If you expected devices from a specific pack, check that it is installed and that the context selects it. The source does not show further steps.
note: The README does not document this message. The cause is inferred from the ListDevices function: devices are skipped when they have sub-items, and the message fires only when no leaf device remains across all selected contexts. Whether the pack list is empty or only contains devices with sub-items is not visible in these lines.

message: no pack was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no pack was found with filter '…'
cause: The csolution pack listing (the list-packs command with a filter argument) builds one entry per installed pack, formatted as the pack ID plus its .pdsc path, or as the locked/available-update text when locked packs are shown. The user's filter string is split into terms and applied to these entries; when no entry matches any term, the message is printed with the filter text in place of '<…>' and the command fails. So the filter did not match any installed pack ID or pack path, or no packs were loaded at all.
fix: Run the same command without a filter to list the installed packs and their IDs, then retry with a filter term that matches a part of an ID or path shown there. If the expected pack is missing from that list, install it (for example with cpackget) or check the pack root and the pack selection used for loading.
note: The README does not document this message. The exact matching rule is in RteUtils::ApplyFilter, which is not in the lines given, so the cause describes the matched text only as far as the lines show. The sibling message for boards uses the same pattern at ProjMgrWorker.cpp:4300-4301.

message: no packs were found for version check
title: csolution: no packs were found for version check
cause: The version check builds a list of results from the packs loaded for the selected contexts (usedPacks, filled from m_loadedPacks in the loop at lines 6150-6167). When no packs were loaded for any selected context, usedPacks stays empty, checkPackResults stays empty, and the tool prints this error and returns false. This means the project's selected contexts resolved to no packs, so there was nothing to compare against the latest installed versions.
fix: Check that the csolution project lists the packs it uses (for example through its components or pack requirements) and that those packs are installed in the CMSIS pack root or in a project-specified pack path. Then rerun the version check on the same project. The source does not show which user input leads to an empty pack list, so verify the pack list for the context you run it on.
note: The README does not document this message. The source shows the trigger as an empty result list, but not which project input causes the list to be empty, so the cause is an inference from the code. The message without a filter is distinct from the filtered variant at line 6209, which adds the filter text.

message: no packs were found for version check with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no packs were found for version check with filter '…'
cause: The version check ran and produced one or more pack result lines, but the filter given on the command line matched none of them. cause: The SVD file declares a peripheral whose address block (base address plus the block's offset and size) extends beyond the 32-bit address space, so the end of the block would wrap past 0xFFFFFFFF. The %NAME% and %ADDR% placeholders are the peripheral name and its base address from the SVD, and %TEXT% describes the offending address block. The source lines were not available, so this is inferred from the message text alone.
fix: Open the SVD file, find the peripheral named in the message and check its baseAddress together with the addressBlock offset and size of its address block; correct the values so the block ends at or below 0xFFFFFFFF, then run svdconv again.
note: Source lines were unavailable; the cause is inferred from the message wording. The fix assumes the peripheral base address or the address block values are wrong in the SVD.

title: svdconv M381: Interrupt '…' Number '…' greater or equal <deviceNumInterrupts>: '…'.
cause: svdconv found an SVD interrupt whose number is greater than or equal to the device's declared interrupt count (deviceNumInterrupts). The %NAME% is the peripheral interrupt name, %NUM% its number, and %NUM2% the device-wide limit it exceeds. The mismatch is between the interrupt numbers in the SVD and the device-level interrupt count given in the description.
fix: Check the SVD: the interrupt value for the named interrupt should be below the device's interrupt count. Either correct the interrupt number in the peripheral entry or raise the device interrupt count (deviceNumInterrupts) so it covers that number, then rerun svdconv.

message: '<…>' contains non-portable backslash, use forward slash instead
title: csolution: '…' contains non-portable backslash, use forward slash instead
cause: The csolution parser checks every path-valued YAML entry (parsed through ParsePortablePath or ParsePortablePaths) for a backslash character. The warning fires when the value of a path key in the csolution YAML files, such as a file, include or directory entry, contains a Windows-style backslash separator. The placeholder in the message is that offending value, copied verbatim from the YAML.
fix: Edit the YAML entry that the warning points to (file and line are given in the log) and replace each backslash with a forward slash, for example write src/main.c instead of src\main.c. Forward slashes work on all host systems, so the project stays portable between Windows and Linux.
note: The message is a warning, not an error, so the build continues. The code is empty in the message, so the id carries no code. The README does not document this message.

title: csolution: '…' has case inconsistency, use '…' instead
cause: EnsurePortability resolves a relative path from a csolution YAML file against the file's parent directory, and if that path exists it compares the lexically normalized form with the filesystem's canonical spelling. When the two differ, the path in the YAML uses different letter case from the actual file or directory on disk, which is not portable to case-sensitive systems. The first placeholder is the value as written in the YAML and the second is the canonical path relative to the parent directory.
fix: Edit the path in the csolution YAML so its letter case matches the file or directory name on disk, using the suggested relative path from the message, for example replacing a path written as Src/Main.c with src/main.c if the disk name is src/main.c. Then rebuild.
note: The check runs only when the path exists, so a missing file produces no case warning. The same EnsurePortability function also emits the backslash and absolute-path warnings, which are separate messages.

message: '<…>' is not selectable as active target-set
title: csolution: '…' is not selectable as active target-set
cause: The value given for the active target (the --active option, as <target-type>@<target-set>) does not match anything declared in the csolution's target-types. PopulateActiveTargetSet splits the string at '@' and looks for a target-type with that name. If none matches, the active target-type stays empty. If the target-type matches but no target-set with the given name exists under it, the lookup also fails. Either way the message prints the whole string the user passed.
fix: Use an active target that exists in the csolution file: a target-type name from target-types, optionally followed by @ and a target-set name listed under that target-type. Check the spelling of both parts against target-types in the csolution YAML. Dropping the @ part selects the target-type alone, provided it is declared.
note: The message is not documented in the README. The empty-string case (--active with no value) takes the first target-type and does not reach this error.

message: '<…>' this linker script is ignored<…>; multiple linker scripts defined<…>
title: csolution: '…' this linker script is ignored…; multiple linker scripts defined…
cause: A file with category linkerScript is added to a context, but the context already has a linker script, or it uses linker autoGen, or it defines linker regions or defines, so the tool keeps the first linker script and ignores this file. The message names the ignored file. The suffix '; multiple linker scripts defined' is added only when a script has already been selected, so it appears when two linker-script files are listed. Without that suffix, the file was ignored because of autoGen, regions or defines.
fix: Keep exactly one linker-script file in the context's file list (for example in the project or layer .csolution.yml). If you list several, remove the extra ones. If you list a linker script together with linker regions or defines, or with linker autoGen, remove one of the two approaches so that the script is used as the linker script.
note: The README does not document this message. The warning fires only in the else branch of the condition at line 3880, and the 'multiple linker scripts defined' suffix depends on context.linker.script being non-empty at that point, so the suffix can be absent even when the ignore reason is autoGen, regions or defines.

message: <…>'device: Dname'<…>'board:' node<…> is deprecated at this level and accepted in *.csolution.yml only
title: csolution: …'device: Dname'…'board:' node… is deprecated at this level and accepted in *.csolution.yml only
cause: The board or device name is set under a target in a *.cproject.yml or *.clayer.yml file. ParseTargetType collects the target's board and device values, and when the file name matches cproject or clayer yml, any non-empty value is reported, except a device written in the form :<processor-name>, which is silently accepted. The <…> placeholder is either the text 'device: Dname' or the 'board:' node, depending on which key is non-empty; the message prints the offending key name, not the value.
fix: Remove the board: or device: entry from the cproject.yml or clayer.yml file and move it to the *.csolution.yml file, where it is accepted. For a device that only selects a processor, write it in the form device: :<processor-name> so the warning is not raised.
note: The message text has a variable part that differs per key: for device it is 'device: Dname' and for board it is 'board:' node. The placeholder <…> in the message is the same text used in the source. The source reports the warning once per non-empty key in each file, so both board and device can produce a warning in the same file.

message: absolute path '<…>' is not portable, use relative path instead
title: csolution: absolute path '…' is not portable, use relative path instead
cause: EnsurePortability runs on path-valued csolution YAML entries (through ParsePortablePath and ParsePortablePaths). When the value is an absolute path, fs::path(value).is_absolute() is true and the tool emits this warning with the offending value in place of the placeholder. The warning is not an error; the build keeps the path as written, but it will not resolve the same on another machine or in a different checkout.
fix: Replace the absolute path in the YAML entry with a path relative to the file that contains it, for example change an absolute directory to a path such as ../lib or ./Source, so that it resolves from the project file location. Re-run csolution to confirm the warning is gone.
note: The warning is emitted with Warn, not Error, so processing continues. The message text is the absolute path '<…>' (the variable part is the raw YAML value). The same function also emits the backslash and case-inconsistency warnings for the same entries; those are distinct messages.

message: access sequence '$Pack(<…>)' must have the format '$Pack(vendor::name)$'
title: csolution: access sequence '$Pack(…)' must have the format '$Pack(vendor::name)$'
cause: The $Pack(...)$ access sequence used in a csolution file does not contain a valid vendor::name pair. ExpandPackDir parses the text between the parentheses with ConvertToPackInfo, and the vendor or the name comes out empty, so the sequence cannot identify a pack. The <…> in the message is the text the user wrote between $Pack( and ).
fix: Rewrite the access sequence so the argument has the form vendor::name, for example $Pack(ARM::CMSIS)$ instead of a bare name without the vendor part. Then run the build again.
note: The warning is raised before the pack is looked up, so it is about the syntax of the argument only. When the syntax is valid but no loaded pack matches, the tool prints a different message ('access sequence pack was not loaded').

title: csolution: board '…' was not found
cause: The board named in the project's board field (the context.board string, which GetBoardItem splits into name, vendor and revision) matches no board in the filtered model's board list. The tool keeps only boards whose name equals the parsed name exactly and, when a vendor was given, whose vendor string also equals it. If nothing passes both checks, it prints this error and fails the context. The board list comes from the packs the tool has loaded, so a board from a pack that is not available to the project also produces this message.
fix: Check the board name and vendor in the csolution board entry against the board's name and vendor as listed in the board pack's PDSC. Remove or correct the vendor part if it does not match exactly. Make sure the pack that provides the board is installed and reachable for the project, for example by listing it under its dependencies in the .csolution.yml or .cproject.yml file. Then run the build again.
note: Message text is also printed at ProjMgrWorker.cpp:1396 when no board matches a given revision; that call omits the context name, and its cause is a revision mismatch, not a missing board. The filtered model's pack selection is not in the lines provided, so the pack-availability part of the cause is inferred from the code that builds the model.

message: build-type '.<…>' does not exist in solution<…>, did you mean '+<…>'?<…>
title: csolution: build-type '.…' does not exist in solution…, did you mean '+…'?…
cause: The csolution run was given a type filter entry with a leading '.' (build-type) whose name matches no build type defined in the solution. The name is collected from the solution's build-types and from their context maps, and CheckTypeFilterSpelling records it as missing from that set. The <…> in the message is the filter's name without the '.' prefix. If the same name exists as a target type, the message adds the hint that the user probably meant the '+' prefix, which selects target types.
fix: Find the filter entry that uses the named type with a '.' prefix and correct it. Use '.<name>' only when <name> is a build type defined in the solution's build-types section. If <name> is a target type, write it as '+<name>' instead, as the hint says. The warning is printed once per missing name in the include and exclude filters.

The '.' and '+' hint is a string check on the name, so a name that exists as both a build type and a target type is never flagged as misspelled. The warning text is built in PrintMissingFilters, which is outside the lines given, but it is read in full from 4095-4096.

message: command line options '--quiet' and '--verbose' are mutually exclusive
title: csolution: command line options '--quiet' and '--verbose' are mutually exclusive
cause: The csolution command line was given both --quiet and --verbose. Both flags set static logger flags (ProjMgrLogger::m_quiet and ProjMgrLogger::m_verbose) during option parsing, and after parsing finishes the code rejects the combination because the two logging levels cannot apply at once. The check runs after the help option is handled and before the load policy is set.
fix: Run the command with only one of the two options: keep --quiet for minimal output or --verbose for detailed output, and remove the other from the command line or from any wrapper script or build step that adds it.
