message: conflict: automatic linker script generation overrules specified script '<…>'
title: csolution: conflict: automatic linker script generation overrules specified script '…'
cause: The linker section of the csolution project sets both an explicit linker script and automatic linker script generation (linker: autoGen). When the tool processes an ELF output that is not image-only and not a West or CMake build, it sees a non-empty linker script together with autoGen enabled, prints this warning and discards the script path, so the generated script is used instead. The text in angle brackets is the script path from the project's linker settings.
fix: Decide which linker script should be used. To keep the generated script, remove the script entry from the linker section of the csolution project so the warning no longer applies. To use your own script, turn off automatic generation (set autoGen to false, or remove it) and keep the script entry.
note: The README does not document this message. The warning is emitted with the context name, so it appears per build context. The exact YAML key names were not visible in the lines given, so the fix refers to the setting by its meaning.

title: csolution: cproject file was not found
cause: The csolution parser lists a cproject entry under `projects` in the csolution file. For each entry, ProjMgr resolves `m_rootDir + "/" + cproject` with `fs::canonical` and ignores the error code. When the path does not exist, canonical returns an empty path, the generic string is empty, and the tool prints this error with the entry as the file argument. The reported path is the entry as written in the csolution file, not the resolved one.
fix: Open the csolution file and check the `projects` entry named in the message. Paths are resolved relative to the directory that contains the csolution file. Correct the path or file name so it points to an existing cproject.yml, for example `- project: ./app/app.cproject.yml` style entries as your layout requires, then run the command again.
note: The README does not document this message. The code prints the message with the raw cproject entry, so the reported text may be a relative path that differs from the resolved location. The error code from fs::canonical is discarded, so the underlying OS reason is not shown; a missing file is the case the code is written for.

title: csolution: cproject.yml filenames must be unique
cause: The csolution file lists more than one cproject in its projects section, and two or more of those entries end in the same file name (for example two entries both pointing at a cproject.yml in different directories). The tool collects only the file name of each listed cproject, sorts them, and fails when any name appears twice. Such a solution cannot be processed because the resulting project names would collide.
fix: Rename the cproject.yml files so that each file name is unique across the solution, for example by giving each project a distinct file name such as app1.cproject.yml and app2.cproject.yml, and update the matching entries under projects in the csolution.yml. Keep each project in its own sub-directory as well, since the tool warns when directories are shared.
note: The message is printed with the csolution file as its file argument. The check compares only file names, so two projects in different directories with the same file name also trigger it; the directory check at line 520 only produces a warning. The README does not document this message.

message: cproject.yml files should be placed in separate sub-directories
title: csolution: cproject.yml files should be placed in separate sub-directories
cause: The csolution file lists more than one cproject, and two or more of them have the same parent directory, so their cproject.yml files are not in separate sub-directories. The check sorts the parent directories of all listed cprojects into a multiset and warns when any directory appears twice. This is a warning only, so processing continues.
fix: Move each cproject.yml into its own sub-directory, so that every project's parent directory is distinct, and update the cprojects entries in the csolution.yml to match. Keeping the same directory and only renaming the file does not clear it, because the check compares directories.
note: Unlike the duplicate filename check at line 516, which is an error, this directory check only warns and the function continues. Duplicate directories are reached only when cprojects.size() is greater than one.

title: csolution: csolution file not specified
cause: PopulateContexts only parses a csolution when m_csolutionFile is non-empty. When it is empty, the tool logs this error and stops. The csolution file path was not set on the command line, so the tool has no solution file to load.
fix: Run csolution again and pass the path to your .csolution.yml file as the input. Check that the path is spelled correctly and that the file exists. The source lines shown do not name the exact command-line option, so confirm the syntax with the csolution help output.
note: The message has no file name or variable part. The check is on the path the tool stores, so it fires when no csolution file was given, not when the file is missing from disk. A missing file is reported by the parser instead.

title: csolution: csolution file was not found
cause: The command line named a csolution file, either as a positional argument ending in .csolution.yml or .csolution.yaml or via the --solution option, and that path does not exist on disk when csolution checks it. The message is printed with the given path as its detail, so the user's path is what is missing or mistyped.
fix: Check the path given on the command line for typos and make sure it is relative to the current working directory or absolute. Confirm the file exists with its full .csolution.yml or .csolution.yaml name, then run the command again, for example: csolution convert -s path/to/project.csolution.yml
note: The README does not document this message. The check runs before the path is canonicalized, so a relative path is tested against the current working directory. The message is printed with the path as its detail argument, which is why the path appears after the message in the log.

message: customization of intermediate directory 'intdir' is ignored by the cbuild2cmake backend
title: csolution: customization of intermediate directory 'intdir' is ignored by the cbuild2cmake backend
cause: The csolution YAML sets an intermediate directory (`directories: intdir:`) at the solution level, but the build is running with the cbuild2cmake backend (m_cbuild2cmake is set). In AddContext the cbuild2cmake path keeps the default intdir of 'tmp' and only emits this warning instead of applying the user's 'intdir' value, so the customization has no effect on the generated context.
fix: Remove the `intdir` entry from the `directories` section of the csolution file if the default intermediate directory is acceptable, or build without the cbuild2cmake backend if the custom 'intdir' must be honoured. The source only shows that the value is ignored; it does not show another supported way to set it under cbuild2cmake.
note: The README does not document this message. The warning fires once per context created while the csolution intdir is non-empty, so it can repeat for each build-type and target-type combination in the log.

title: csolution: device '…' does not support '…: …'
cause: The user's csolution YAML sets an endian value (the `endian` key of the processor or device selection) for a device whose pack fixes its endianness to a different value. At ProjMgrWorker.cpp:1603-1607 the tool reads the device's target attribute for RTE_DENDIAN, and if it is not the configurable value and differs from the value the user requested, it prints this warning. The `<…>` device is the device name from the context, and the `endian: <…>` part is the user's requested value.
fix: Remove the `endian` setting from the csolution YAML so the device default applies, or set it to the endianness the device supports. If the project needs the requested endianness, select a device or variant whose pack declares that endianness.
note: The message is a warning, not an error, so the build continues with the device's fixed endianness. The printed text does not name the device's supported value. The same message format is also used for fpu, dsp, mve, trustzone and branch-protection checks at lines 1617 and 1632-1633, so the text alone does not identify which attribute failed beyond the key shown. The id has no code in the message header.

title: csolution: duplicate CMake image type '…'
cause: A csolution project's CMake descriptor lists more than one entry under 'images' with the same 'type' value. The parser keeps a set of the type strings it has seen in that images list and rejects the second occurrence; the '<…>' in the message is the repeated type string taken from the 'type' key of the image entry.
fix: Open the csolution YAML file named in the log and find the 'cmake' project entry with an 'images' list. Give each image a distinct 'type' value, or remove the duplicate image entry, then run csolution again.
note: The error is reported at the line of the 'type' key of the duplicate image entry, and the function returns false, which aborts parsing of the csolution file. The message is not documented in the README.

title: csolution: executing generator '…' for context '…' failed
cause: csolution runs the generator's command line (built at line 5163) through CrossPlatformUtils::ExecCommand from the generator's working directory. The message is printed when that process returns a non-zero exit status, so the generator itself reported a failure. The generator's own output was logged just before at Info level as "generator '<id>' for context '<context>' reported:", and that output holds the actual error. The placeholders are the generator ID and the selected context name.
fix: Read the output printed by the preceding "reported:" Info line and fix the problem it describes, such as missing inputs or a bad generator configuration. To reproduce, run the generator's expanded command line by hand from the generator's working directory (the directory csolution changes into before running it) and check its exit code. After fixing the cause, rerun the csolution command.
note: The message carries no detail of its own; the useful information is the generator output logged at line 5174. The README does not document this message.

title: csolution: file doesn't exist: '…'
cause: csolution calls ProjMgrYamlSchemaChecker::Validate with the path of a YAML input file before it runs schema validation. The check at line 21 uses RteFsUtils::Exists on that path, and when no file exists there the tool logs this error with the path as given, in the placeholder, and returns false. The path is whatever was passed to the tool, so the missing file is the one named in the message.
fix: Check the file name and path in the message for typos or a wrong extension, and confirm that the file exists at that location. If the path is relative, run csolution from the directory that contains it, or pass the absolute path. Then run the command again.
note: The source lines do not show which callers pass which file, so the exact file that is missing is known only from the placeholder in the message. The message is not documented in the README.

message: file is missing and required due to use of --frozen-packs option
title: csolution: file is missing and required due to use of --frozen-packs option
cause: The csolution tool was run with the --frozen-packs option, which requires the pack set to be fixed by an existing cbuild-pack file. ParseCsolution derives the expected name by replacing the .csolution.yml suffix of the input with .cbuild-pack.yml; when that file does not exist and frozenPacks is set, the tool prints this error with that expected path as the file and stops. The file is missing because the packs have not been resolved and written to a cbuild-pack file yet, or the file is located elsewhere than the csolution file.
fix: Generate the cbuild-pack file next to the csolution file before running with --frozen-packs, for example by running the csolution command without --frozen-packs once (for instance a pack resolution or build run) so the cbuild-pack.yml is written, then rerun with --frozen-packs. Alternatively, drop --frozen-packs if you do not need a fixed pack set. Check that the file named in the message sits beside the .csolution.yml file.
note: The message has no code and is not documented in the README. The fix to generate the cbuild-pack file by an earlier run is an inference from the source, since the source only checks for the file's existence; the source does not show which command writes it.

title: csolution: input csolution.yml was not specified
cause: The csolution command ran its pack version check mode without a csolution.yml path. RunCheckPackVerCmd requires m_csolutionFile to be set before it parses contexts, and it stops with this error when that input is empty. Unlike the list-toolchains path, which only parses files when a csolution file was given, this check always needs one.
fix: Run the same csolution command again and pass the path to your csolution.yml project file as its input argument, for example csolution <check-pack-version-subcommand> path/to/project.csolution.yml. Use the subcommand that runs the pack version check; the source lines shown do not name it.
note: The README does not document this message. The fix relies on the subcommand's own argument syntax, which is outside the lines given, so the example command is generic.

message: invalid arguments: '-a' option cannot be used in combination with '-S'
title: csolution: invalid arguments: '-a' option cannot be used in combination with '-S'
cause: The csolution command line combined the target-set option '-a' with '-S' (the cbuild-set selection path). ParseContextSelection checks the cbuild-set flag first and rejects the call whenever a target type was given with '-a' (m_activeTargetType is non-empty), so the two options cannot be used together.
fix: Run csolution with either '-a' (to select a target type and its contexts) or '-S' (to process the contexts stored in the cbuild-set file), but not both in the same invocation. If you want the cbuild-set contexts, drop '-a'; if you want the target-set contexts, drop '-S'.
note: The message text is not in the README. The check is the first branch, so '-a' with '-S' fails before any context is parsed. The fix relies on the else-if ordering shown in the lines given; the meaning of each flag is inferred from the branch bodies.

title: csolution: invalid define: …, improper quotes
cause: A define value in a csolution YAML file (the defines list of a project, component or similar node) contains double-quote characters that do not form a single correctly quoted pair. The validator counts the quotes in the value; if the count is not zero and not exactly two, or if the two quotes do not sit at both ends (either as a plain " ... " wrapper or as an escaped \" ... \" wrapper), the value is rejected. The <…> in the message is the define value as written in the YAML.
fix: Find the define named in the message and correct its quoting so that it has either no double quotes or exactly one pair wrapping the whole value, for example: defines: [ MY_STRING: "hello" ] (or a plain value without quotes). Remove stray or embedded quotes, or escape them so the value starts and ends with the quote pair. Then run the csolution command again.
note: The message prints the whole define value; for map-style defines the value checked is the map value only, not the key. The check runs per define item and the function returns false, so the error is printed once per invalid value.

title: csolution: key '…' was not recognized
cause: The csolution YAML parser checks every key in a mapping against the set of keys allowed for that node (the root or a sequence/mapping entry it validates recursively). The key named in the message is not in the allowed set for the node where it appears, which usually means a typo, a key placed at the wrong nesting level, or a key that the installed tool version does not know. The message is a warning, so parsing continues with the unrecognized key ignored.
fix: Find the key named in the message in your csolution YAML (project, layer or cbuild-pack file) and check its spelling and indentation against the schema of the node it sits under. Remove the key or move it to the node where it belongs. If the key is valid for your tool version but still flagged, update csolution to a version that knows it.
note: The message text is '<key> was not recognized' with the key quoted; the id is the same family as the message. Nested nodes are validated through ValidateSequence and ValidateMapping, so the reported key can belong to any level of the file.

title: csolution: list <args> was not found
cause: The csolution `list` command takes one subcommand word, which the tool stores in m_args. The value the user gave is not one of the keys in the handler map built in ProcessListCommand, so the lookup fails and the tool prints this error. The message text is a literal string in the source, so the `<args>` in it does not show the value the user typed.
fix: Run `csolution list` with one of the supported subcommands: packs, boards, devices, npus, components, configs, dependencies, examples, templates, contexts, targets, target-sets, debuggers, generators, layers, toolchains or environment. For example: `csolution list packs`. Check the spelling of the word you passed; the match is exact and case-sensitive.
note: The message does not repeat the unknown value, so the user has to compare their command with the list above. The sibling message at ProjMgr.cpp:415-418 covers the case where no subcommand is given. The README does not document this message.

title: csolution: list <args> was not specified
cause: The user ran `csolution list` without the sub-command argument that says what to list. ProcessListCommand() checks m_args before doing anything else and, when it is empty, prints this error and returns ERROR. The <args> placeholder stands for the missing item; valid values are the keys of the handler map in the same function (packs, boards, devices, npus, components, configs, dependencies, examples, templates, contexts, targets, target-sets, debuggers, generators, layers, toolchains, environment).
fix: Run the list command with one of the supported arguments, for example `csolution list packs` or `csolution list devices`. Choose the name that matches the information you need; the source lists the accepted names in the handler map of ProcessListCommand().
note: The sibling message for an unknown argument is 'list <args> was not found' (ProjMgr.cpp:441). The README does not document this message, so the cause and fix come from the source alone.

message: mlops.npu.macs value does not match DFP device information
title: csolution: mlops.npu.macs value does not match DFP device information
cause: The csolution sets an mlops.npu.macs value (after variable expansion) and the DFP device information lists NPU entries for the selected processors, but none of those entries has a matching MACs count. The comparison strips the "MACs" suffix from the DFP values and compares them numerically; when the NPU type is also set, the entry must additionally have that same type. So the user's macs value (or the macs/type pair) does not correspond to any NPU the device's pack provides.
fix: Check the mlops.npu.macs value in the csolution YAML against the NPU configurations the selected device's DFP offers, and correct it to a listed MACs count. Alternatively remove mlops.npu.macs so the tool picks the matching value from the DFP when mlops.npu.type is set or from the first NPU entry when neither is set. If mlops.npu.type is also set, make sure the type and MACs describe the same NPU.
note: The message is not documented in the README. The sibling message for mlops.npu.type is printed at line 283 under the same condition style. The warning only fires when the DFP provides NPU info items for the device's pnames, so it does not appear for devices without NPU data.

message: mlops.npu.type value does not match DFP device information
title: csolution: mlops.npu.type value does not match DFP device information
cause: The csolution sets an NPU type under mlops.npu.type that matches no NPU entry of the Device Family Pack (DFP) for the target device. The tool collects the NPU info items of the DFP for the selected processors (pnames), keeps the ones whose pname matches, and warns when none of them has the type the user gave. The type is taken from the solution after $...$ variable expansion, so a value that expands to something unexpected also triggers it.
fix: Set mlops.npu.type to one of the NPU types the DFP advertises for the device, or omit mlops.npu.type and let the tool choose the default from the DFP, or set mlops.npu.macs and let the tool find the matching type. Check the spelling against the DFP device description and confirm the device and processor are correct and the DFP is installed.
note: The README does not document this message. The fix list is derived from the source: when type is empty the tool picks a default, and when only macs is given it looks up the type from macs. The code does not state the exact accepted type names.

title: csolution: mlops: target type '…' not found
cause: The MLOps item in the csolution YAML names a target-type that is not declared under the csolution's target-types section. ResolveTargetSet searches csolution.targetTypes by name, and when the requested target.targetType matches none of the declared names, FindTargetType returns false and the error is printed with the requested name substituted for the placeholder.
fix: Check the target-type name used by the mlops entry against the target-types declared in the csolution file and make them match exactly, since the comparison is a plain string equality. Either correct the mlops reference or add a matching target-type declaration to the csolution. If the mlops entry does not need a specific target-type, leave its target-type empty so the tool selects a declared one.
note: The message has no code and the README does not document it. The fallback branch when the target-type is empty returns true even when no target set was found, which the source handles separately and is not part of this message.

message: no NPU was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no NPU was found with filter '…'
cause: The NPU listing collected at least one installed NPU, but none of them matched the filter string the user passed, so the result list is empty. A filter word counts as matched if it appears in the NPU description line. Otherwise it must match one of that NPU's device lines, and the NPU is dropped if no device line matches. The '<…>' in the message is the filter text as given by the user.
fix: Check the filter words for typos or for names that do not appear in the NPU or device descriptions, then retry with a broader filter. To see every installed NPU, run the same listing command without the filter argument.
note: This message is only reached when a non-empty filter was given, because without a filter every collected NPU is added. The separate message 'no installed NPU was found' at line 4386 covers the case where no NPU is installed at all. The README does not document this message.

message: no device was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no device was found with filter '…'
cause: The csolution device listing (ListDevices) was run with a filter argument, and none of the installed devices (vendor::name (pack) entries built from the loaded packs) matched the filter terms. The '<…>' in the message is the filter string the user passed on the command line.
fix: Check the filter spelling against the listing without a filter, for example by running the same list-devices command with no filter argument and searching the output for the device name or vendor. Install the pack that provides the device if it is missing (csolution list packs or the cpackget tool can show installed packs), then rerun with a corrected filter.
note: Message is not listed in the README. The filter is applied with RteUtils::ApplyFilter to the list of installed devices; if no packs are installed the earlier 'no installed device was found' error is printed instead.

message: no target-set was found with filter '<…>'
title: csolution: no target-set was found with filter '…'
cause: The csolution command was given a filter (for listing target-sets) and none of the target-set names built from the csolution's target-types match it. Each target-set is listed as its target-type name, with '@' and the set name appended when the set is non-empty, and the filter is matched against these names with RteUtils::ApplyFilter. The '<…>' in the message is the filter text as the user passed it.
fix: Check the target-type and target-set names defined in the csolution.yml under target-types, then rerun the listing with a filter that matches them, for example the bare target-type name or name@set. Omit the filter to list all target-sets.
note: The message is not listed in the README. The sibling message for contexts ('no context was found with filter') uses the same pattern at ProjMgrWorker.cpp:4843; this entry covers only the target-set listing path.

message: number must be integer or hexadecimal prefixed by 0x
title: csolution: number must be integer or hexadecimal prefixed by 0x
cause: ProjMgrYamlParser::ParseNumber reads a numeric csolution YAML field as a string and checks it against the pattern ^(0x[0-9a-fA-F]+)$ or ^([0-9]*)$. The warning is printed when the value in the YAML is neither a run of decimal digits nor a 0x-prefixed hexadecimal number, for example a negative number, a decimal fraction, a value with a suffix or spaces, or a non-hex value after 0x. The warning gives the location of the value in the file, but not the key or the value itself, so the user has to find the offending entry at that line and column.
fix: Open the YAML file at the line and column given in the warning and rewrite the value as a plain decimal integer (for example 4096) or as a hexadecimal number with the 0x prefix and hex digits only (for example 0x1000). Remove any sign, decimal point, unit suffix, or surrounding text from the value.
note: The message does not name the key or the value, so a reviewer should know the user must locate the entry from the reported line and column. The regex also accepts an empty value, so an empty number produces no warning. The value is kept as a string and parsing continues after the warning; the source here does not show what happens to the non-matching value downstream, and the callers of ParseNumber are not in the lines given. The README has no entry for this message.

message: output 'lib' is incompatible with other output types
title: csolution: output 'lib' is incompatible with other output types
cause: The project's output types, collected from the output type entries of the project and its matching setups and from cmake image types, include lib together with at least one of elf, hex or bin. The source checks this combination in ProcessOutputFilenames and refuses it, because a library output cannot be combined with an executable-style output in the same context. The 'output' type list in the csolution YAML (project or setup level) or the image types supplied through cmake are the inputs that produce the conflict.
fix: Keep only one output family for the context: either set the output type to lib alone, or remove lib and keep elf, hex and/or bin. Check the output type entries of the project and of every setup whose filters match the current context, and the cmake image types if cmake images are used, since any of them can add an output type. Re-run the csolution command after editing.
note: The README does not document this message. The check runs after setup and cmake output types are merged, so the conflicting type may come from a setup or a cmake image rather than the top-level output list. The default elf output is only added later and does not cause this error.

title: csolution: pack path: … does not exist
cause: A pack entry in the csolution project files has a `path` that points to a local pack folder, and that path does not exist once it is resolved against the csolution file's directory. The message prints the path exactly as written in the project file (`packageEntry.path`), so `<…>` is that raw value. The check runs on the normalized copy, so a relative path is judged from the csolution directory, not from the current working directory.
fix: Open the csolution or project file that lists the pack and find the `path` value named in the message. Make it relative to that file's directory, or use an absolute path, so that it points to the folder that contains the pack's .pdsc file. Confirm the folder exists on disk, then run the build again. The folder must also contain `<vendor>.<name>.pdsc`, or the tool stops with a different error about a missing pdsc file.
note: The message is not documented in the README. The printed path is the unresolved value from the project file, not the resolved absolute path that was tested, so the user has to resolve it relative to the csolution directory to see what the tool checked. The code field is empty in the catalog entry.

message: pdsc file was not found in: <…>
title: csolution: pdsc file was not found in: …
cause: A project-local pack entry (a pack item with a path, in the csolution pack list) points to a directory that exists, but the expected PDSC file is not in it. The tool builds the name as <vendor>.<name>.pdsc from the pack's vendor and name and looks for it inside the path. The message prints the configured path (<…>) of that pack entry.
fix: Check the pack entry's path and the pack identity it is given. The directory named by the path must contain a file named <vendor>.<name>.pdsc, where vendor and name match the pack entry (for example Keil.STM32F4xx_DFP.pdsc for vendor Keil and name STM32F4xx_DFP). Rename the PDSC file or correct the vendor/name in the pack entry so they agree, or correct the path to the directory that holds the PDSC.
note: The check uses the vendor and name from the pack entry, so a mismatch in those fields produces the same message even when a PDSC file exists in the directory under another name. The message prints packageEntry.path, not the full resolved path, so the user has to match it to the entry in the project file.

message: pname '<…>' does not match any device pname
title: csolution: pname '…' does not match any device pname
cause: The csolution YAML has a `debugger: telnet:` entry whose pname key does not name any processor of the device in the current build context. The pnames map is built from the device's processors; the telnet key is taken from the user's debugger telnet definitions. The placeholder in the message is that key as the user wrote it. The entry is skipped and the build continues with a warning.
fix: Check the telnet entry in the csolution YAML (under the debugger/telnet section of the project or context). Make its key equal to a processor name of the selected device, for example a pname as listed in the device's processor definitions in the PDSC. If the entry is not needed, remove it.
note: The README does not document this message. The check at line 495 runs after the multicore check at line 491, so a multi-core device with an empty telnet pname is reported by the earlier message instead. The fix assumes the device's pnames are the valid keys, which the code implies through the pnames map argument.

title: csolution: processor name '…' was not found
cause: The csolution run resolved the device to a single matched device, but the processor name given in the device item (the pname from the project's device/processor selection) does not match any processor declared for that device in the installed pack. The message quotes that requested processor name. The lookup is done by matchedDevice->GetProcessor(deviceItem.pname) and the error is raised only when a non-empty name was requested and no processor was found.
fix: Check the processor name you set for the device in the csolution YAML (the processor/name entry under the device) against the processors the device defines in its pack (the PDSC device entry). Correct the spelling or choose one of the processor names the device actually declares, then run csolution again. If the processor name is meant to be omitted, remove it so the tool lists the available processors instead.
note: The sibling branch for an empty pname lists the valid processors via 'one of the following processors must be specified', which is a useful hint for the user. The README does not document this message.

message: project descriptors 'project', 'west', and 'cmake' are mutually exclusive
title: csolution: project descriptors 'project', 'west', and 'cmake' are mutually exclusive
cause: The csolution YAML has a single entry under 'projects' that sets more than one of the descriptor keys 'project', 'west' and 'cmake' at once. The parser counts how many of these keys are defined on that entry and rejects the entry when the count is greater than one, because each projects entry may describe only one kind of project.
fix: Split the entry so that each item under 'projects' uses only one of the keys. For example, keep 'project: <path>.cproject.yml' in one list item and move the 'west:' or 'cmake:' block into a separate list item, instead of putting them side by side in the same item.
note: The message text names the three keys directly; the check is a plain count of defined keys on each projects entry, so the cause and fix follow from the source. The README does not document this message.

message: specified device '<…>' is not among board mounted devices
title: csolution: specified device '…' is not among board mounted devices
cause: The project names a device (deviceItem.name) that exists in the installed packs, and it also selects a board whose mounted-device list is non-empty. The device name is not among that board's mounted devices, so the check at line 1489 fails and the tool prints the warning. The placeholder in the message is the full device name, optionally prefixed with the vendor. The build continues because this is only a warning.
fix: Either set the device in the project to one of the devices the board mounts, or remove the device setting so csolution uses the board's mounted device (lines 1495-1500 apply the board device when no device is named). To find the valid names, check the board's mounted devices in its pack description.
note: The message is a warning, not an error, so processing continues with the specified device. The README does not document this message.

message: target-type '+<…>' does not exist in solution<…>, did you mean '.<…>'?<…>
title: csolution: target-type '+…' does not exist in solution…, did you mean '.…'?…
cause: A type filter selects a target-type '+X' that the solution does not define, so the name is not in the solution's target-type list. CheckTypeFilterSpelling sets the 'misspelled' flag when that same name is a build-type, so the user has written the wrong prefix for a name that exists as a build-type. Only the name in the message is known from the source; the filter's origin (context selector or command-line filter) is not shown in the given lines.
fix: Replace the '+X' filter with '.X' wherever the filter is written, so the name is matched as a build-type. Then rerun the build. If X is meant as a target-type, define it in the solution's target-types or correct its spelling so it matches a defined target-type.
note: The warning appears only when the name is misspelled as a target-type and the same name is a known build-type; otherwise the suggestion part is omitted. The message ends with '<…>' in the template, which is the solution name or a trailing context part, not a separate clause. The message code is empty in the catalog entry.

message: type '<…>': it must start with '.' or '+' for normal strings and with '^' or '\' for regex patterns
title: csolution: type '…': it must start with '.' or '+' for normal strings and with '^' or '\' for regex patterns
cause: GetTypes parses one entry of a forContext or notForContext list (ParseTypeFilter, ParseTypePair). It finds the first '.', the first '+' and the first '^' or '\' in the entry, and rejects the entry when none of the three sits at position 0. An entry such as 'Debug' with no prefix, or one where the delimiter is not the first character, matches this case. The '<…>' in the message is that entry as written in the project YAML.
fix: Edit the entry so it starts with the marker for its kind: '.' followed by the build type (for example '.Debug'), '+' followed by the target type (for example '+CM4'), or '^' or '\' followed by a regex pattern. Apply this to each item in the forContext or notForContext list that the message names. Example: forContext: [".Debug", "+CM4"]
note: The condition tests '> 0' on the find results, so std::string::npos (not found) also passes it. An entry that contains no marker at all therefore fails, which is the usual way to hit this message. The message says 'for normal strings' and the README does not document it, so the wording is only a hint. Parsing of a normal string starting with '.' or '+' continues at lines 725-738, which is not shown here.

message: unknown load option: '<…>', it must be 'latest', 'all' or 'required'
title: csolution: unknown load option: '…', it must be 'latest', 'all' or 'required'
cause: The csolution tool was given a load-packs policy value (from the command-line option that sets m_loadPacksPolicy) that is none of the accepted keywords. SetLoadPacksPolicy accepts an empty value (default policy), 'latest', 'all' or 'required' and maps each to a LoadPacksPolicy; any other string falls through to the error, which prints the rejected value in place of the placeholder.
fix: Re-run the command with the load option set to one of the accepted values: 'latest', 'all' or 'required'. Check the spelling and case of the value passed to the option, and omit the option to get the default policy.
note: The trigger line shown is one branch of the chain; the error itself is at ProjMgr.cpp:478. The option name that carries the value is not visible in the given lines, so the exact command-line flag is not stated here. The README does not document this message.

title: csolution: variable '…' redefined from '…' to '…'
cause: ParseContextLayers copies user variables into context.variables in three scopes, in this order: the target build variables, the build-type variables and the target-type variables. Before that, ProjMgrWorker seeds the same map with built-in variables (solution, project, build type, target type and target set). The warning fires when a key is already present with a different expanded value. The first '<…>' is the variable name, the second is the earlier value and the third is the value that replaces it. The usual causes are a csolution variable whose name matches a built-in variable, or the same variable name set to different values in more than one of the scopes that apply to the context.
fix: Give each user variable a name that does not match a built-in variable, and define a variable with one value in only one scope (target build, build type or target type). If the same value is intended in several scopes, make the values identical. Check the variables of the build type and target type that apply to the context named in the message, and the variables under the target build. The later scope's value is the one used, so remove the duplicate you do not want.
note: The README does not document this message. The warning is only printed when the two values differ; identical redefinitions are silent. The built-in variable names come from RteConstants, which is not among the lines given, so the exact names that collide are not listed here. The 'from' value is the earlier value in context.variables, which may be a built-in value rather than a user value.
